title: Statistically secure uncloneable encryption of arbitrary messages
authors: Archishna Bhattacharyya, Anne Broadbent, Eric Culf
abstract: Unconditional uncloneable encryption of a single bit with efficient encryption and decryption is now possible. However, whether the extension to messages of arbitrary length achieves statistical security remains to be known. Using the fact that the encoding bases for the single-bit scheme known to be secure consist of a subset of the Clifford unitaries, we show that this scheme can be upgraded to achieve unconditional uncloneable encryption for messages of arbitrary length, with encoding time polynomial in the message length and security parameter. This establishes that one-time uncloneable encryption of arbitrary messages enjoys statistical security.
summary: This paper proves that uncloneable encryption schemes can be extended from single bits to messages of arbitrary length while maintaining statistical security. By leveraging the structure of Clifford unitaries, the authors establish unconditional security for these multi-message protocols. This advances the theoretical understanding of information security in quantum communication.
main_problem: To establish that one-time uncloneable encryption of messages of arbitrary length maintains statistical security (unconditional security).
main_result: The authors successfully upgrade the single-bit scheme to achieve unconditional uncloneable encryption for arbitrarily long messages, with polynomial encoding time.
method: They extend known secure single-bit schemes by exploiting structural properties of Clifford unitaries and relating cloning bounds across different message lengths using group theory arguments.
model_or_system: The work analyzes Quantum Encryption Schemes (QECM) based on the Clifford group unitaries ($C_n$), focusing on security against cloning and distinguishing attacks.
key_observables: Cloning Value ($c(Q)$) and Cloning-Distinguishing Value ($	ext{cd}(Q)$).
main_assumptions: The extension relies on the structural properties of the Clifford group and prior results concerning unconditional security for single bits.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon established single-bit uncloneable encryption, then develops methods using observable overlap in Measurement-of-Evidence (MoE) games to prove bounds on $	ext{cd}(Q)$ for arbitrary message lengths.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum cryptography, the rigorous mathematical techniques involving group theory and bounding expectation values are highly relevant to understanding information processing limits in open quantum systems.
